newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals slip after mixed opening.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals slip after mixed opening.

text.p: COMEX precious metals futures slipped back in the first hour of trade, after an opening which initially saw gold and silver higher, while NYMEX platinum group metals (PGM) futures continued to slide lower.
"After the run up yesterday, silver saw some fund selling, despite the lower stocks, though the trade provided some support around $4.68 as usual," one floor trader said.
COMEX July silver was down 5.2 cents at $4.710 an ounce after the first hour, reversing Tuesday's gains.
July silver has been in a $4.65-4.90 range since mid-May, with good industrial demand seen below $4.70 and ample supply seen near $4.90, analysts said.

COMEX silver stocks fell a further 2,986,381 ounces to 185,003,689 ounces in data released late Tuesday, the lowest level in several months, after falling 3,500,592 ounces Monday. Earlier silver stocks had climbed to over 200 million ounces in May.

Silver is still seen having slightly better fundamentals than gold, without the overhang of potential central bank sales to cap the market, as silver enters the ninth year of a shortfall between world silver mine production and fabrication demand.
COMEX August gold was up 40 cents at $344.10 an ounce, with the weak downtrend since early May still seen intact, though support has held three times around $343.00 an ounce, analysts noted.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $341.80/30 early, compared to the London Wednesday morning fix at $342.05 and the New York close Tuesday around $341.50/00.
In overnight news the Japanese trade surplus for May surged more than 200 pct over the May 1996 surplus, putting pressure onthe U.S. dollar which helped gold, traders said.
While the revised European Union treaty signed Monday, suggested that longer term the new euro currency may not be a strong one which may also help gold, traders said.
On a negative note though, the Swiss parliament approved a revised charter for the Swiss central bank, allowing it to start lending gold to improve its earnings.
The charter also reduced the amount of gold the Swiss National Bank must hold to cover its notes in circulation to 25 percent from 40 percent.
NYMEX July platinum was down $4.10 at $407.00 an ounce, a ten day low, while NYMEX September palladium was off $6.90 at $171.00.
Funds were continuing to liquidate long positions in July platinum ahead of the contract's delivery period starting in two weeks, traders said.
Open interest in July platinum fell to 10,445 contracts Monday this week, equivalent to 522,250 ounces still outstanding against NYMEX platinum stocks of 54,700 ounces.
In the physical market, one month lease rates for platinum remained around 50 pct and for palladium around 100 pct, while the market waited for Russian supplies resume in late June.

In overnight news, the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) said it was in discussions with the London Platinum and Palladium Market Association about restoring orderly trading conditions to the PGM market.

A senior TOCOM official also said TOCOM would introduce position limits for platinum futures of 600 lots per individual investor in the spot month. Positions in the second delivery month would be limited to 1200 lots.
The London Platinum and Palladium Market had also contacted the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX), TOCOM officials said.
((Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, 212-859-1641))
